Heads Up
HEDZ UP
interjection / noun (Boomer slang)
Heads up! — look up, watch out — has been a shouted warning since at least the early twentieth century (on ships, building sites, and ball fields). The adjective heads-up, alert or clever ("heads-up play"), is mid-century sports slang; the noun a heads-up, advance notice or a warning ("Thanks for the heads-up"), spread in the 1970s–80s and is now standard workplace English.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Heads up! is a warning: look up, something is coming. A heads-up is advance notice: "Just giving you a heads-up — the meeting moved." The Christian observation: Scripture is full of heads-ups, and the people who give them are called watchmen. God told Ezekiel, "I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; therefore thou shalt hear the word at my mouth, and warn them from me" (Eze 33:7), and He laid a heavy responsibility on the watchman who saw danger and stayed silent: "if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned ... his blood will I require at the watchman’s hand" (Eze 33:6). The Lord Jesus gave His whole church a standing heads-up: "what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch" (Mar 13:37). Proverbs praises the man who heeds it: "A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished" (Pro 22:3). And there is a sweeter heads-up in the Gospel too: when the signs of the end appear, "then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh" (Luk 21:28). The Christian’s head is lifted not only in watchfulness but in hope, because the One coming is his Redeemer. David knew Him: "thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head" (Psa 3:3). A father is his family’s watchman. He gives heads-ups about danger — and he teaches his children to lift up their heads in hope.

Webster 1828 Definition

A shouted warning (early 20th c.), then sports slang for alert play and, from the 1970s–80s, "advance notice" — the watchman’s duty of Eze 33:7, and the hopeful command, "look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh" (Luk 21:28).

HEADS UP, interj. (early 20th c.–) Look out! Pay attention! HEADS-UP, n. (1970s–80s) Advance notice; a warning: "Thanks for the heads-up." adj. (sports, mid-20th c.) Alert, quick-witted: "a heads-up play."

Webster (1828) — HEAD, noun hed. 1. The uppermost part of the human body, or the foremost part of the body of prone and creeping animals. This part of the human body contains the organs of hearing, seeing, tasting and smelling; it contains also the brain, which is supposed to be the seat of the intellectual powers, and of sensation. Hence the head is the chief or more important part, and is used for the whole person, in the phrase, let the evil fall on my head

Decode for families: the best heads-up a parent gives is the one Ezekiel was told to give — early, clear, and from God’s Word.

Key Scripture

Eze 33:7 — "So thou, O son of man, I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; therefore thou shalt hear the word at my mouth, and warn them from me."

Eze 33:6 — "But if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, and the people be not warned; if the sword come, and take any person from among them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at the watchman's hand."

Mar 13:37 — "And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch."

Pro 22:3 — "A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished."

Luk 21:28 — "And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh."

Psa 3:3 — "But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head."

Modern Corruption

A useful, wholesome phrase; Scripture fills it with the watchman’s duty to warn and the believer’s privilege to lift up his head in hope of redemption.

expand to see more

There is nothing to correct in heads up. If anything, it rebukes a culture that has grown reluctant to warn. Parents hesitate to give their grown children a heads-up about a bad relationship or a dangerous habit; pastors hesitate to warn about sin; friends stay silent to avoid awkwardness. Ezekiel 33 says silence is not neutral: the watchman who sees the sword and says nothing shares the guilt.

Scripture’s heads-up has two tones. One is warning: watch, the danger is real (Mar 13:37). The other is hope: look up, your redemption is near (Luk 21:28). A Christian home should hear both — a father who will tell his children the truth about danger, and who will also lift up their heads with the promise of Christ’s return.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English héafod (head) + up → early-20th-c. warning heads up! → mid-century sports adj. heads-up → 1970s–80s noun a heads-up (advance notice).

Mid-20th-c. sports slang: heads-up (adj.) — alert, smart

1970s–80s: a heads-up (n.) — advance notice, a warning

Hebrew tsopheh — watchman (Eze 33:6–7); Greek epairo kephalas — "lift up your heads" (Luk 21:28)
